page_title: Traits of a senior software engineer

sources.entry: Traits of a senior software engineer: impact, perception, visibility, influence, mentoring

summary.title: Traits of a senior software engineer
summary.one_liner: Senior engineer promotion depends less on technical depth and more on five traits: impact, perception (reliability), visibility, influence, and mentoring.
takeaways: Seniority is judged mainly by impact: prioritize work that best supports the team and product needs.
Reliability builds perception; doing what you commit to, with care, earns trust and higher-impact goals from your manager.
Make your work visible to the team, adjacent teams, the business, and management, since good work alone may not get noticed.
Influence comes from persuasive, clear communication backed by data, not from title or authority.
Senior engineers scale themselves by mentoring others, freeing their own time for bigger work.
summary.summary: A short opinion piece by Sérgio Martins, a Senior Test Engineer, written after his promotion to senior. He argues that technical skill is necessary but not sufficient for seniority and lists five traits: impact, perception, visibility, influence, and mentoring, each with a brief explanation and a supporting quote. The comments add points such as facilitation, teamwork, and that seniority is about team professionalism rather than how many languages one knows. It is a personal essay with general advice rather than a step-by-step guide.
